title: Buy Electronics Online in Pakistan Without Getting a Brick in a Box
author: Omar Farooq
authorBio: Founder of BazaarNow. Has bought enough electronics online to know exactly which red flags mean 'run.' Once received a 'power bank' that was just two AA batteries in a plastic shell. Still bitter.
excerpt: 259+ electronics products, zero bricks. How to buy gadgets online in Pakistan without getting scammed, which categories are safe, and when paying in advance actually saves you 5%.

sections.content: Buying electronics online in Pakistan is the shopping equivalent of driving in Lahore — the road is fine, but the surprises come from what other people do. You'll find genuine AirPods and fake AirPods on the same page. You'll see a 10,000 mAh power bank for Rs. 400 that is, I guarantee you, two AA batteries and some gravel in a plastic shell. The good news: once you know the rules, it's actually safer than buying from a shop where the guy won't let you open the box until you've paid. At least online you have COD. And a return policy. And the ability to name and shame. Publicly. On the store's WhatsApp.

sections.text: The three rules of buying electronics online that will save you from every scam

items: Never pay in advance on your first order from a store. Ever. COD exists for electronics shopping. Use it. The Rs. 100 delivery rider tip is cheaper than losing Rs. 4,500 on fake AirPods.

If the price is more than 30% below market average, walk away. A genuine Samsung 25W charger costs Rs. 1,800-2,200 in Pakistan. If someone's selling it for Rs. 600, what you're buying is a charger-shaped object. It will charge your phone for approximately 12 seconds before emitting a sound that can only be described as 'fzzzzt.'

Check the product images. Specifically: are they stock photos from the brand's official website, or are they actual photos of the product? Stock photos from the brand ≠ the seller has the genuine item. Real photos taken by the seller = at minimum, they physically possess something. (Whether that something works is the next question. But at least something exists.)

sections.text: AirPods, watches, and chargers — what's actually worth buying online

sections.content: Not every electronics category is equally safe for online shopping. Here's the honest breakdown based on what we've seen at BazaarNow across thousands of orders.

sections.text: Wireless earbuds and audio — safest category, highest volume

sections.content: Earbuds are the easiest electronics product to buy online because the technology is now mature. Bluetooth 5.3 chips cost under Rs. 200 at wholesale. A decent pair of wireless earbuds with ANC can be manufactured for under Rs. 1,500. This means the Rs. 3,000-5,000 range is genuinely good quality — not fake, just Chinese OEM with Pakistani branding. Look for models that specify the Bluetooth version (5.3 or newer), battery life in hours (not 'long lasting'), and driver size in mm. Our electronics category has 30+ earbud options with actual specs listed — because 'good sound quality' is not a specification. It's a wish.

sections.text: Smartwatches — know the difference between a watch and a fitness band

sections.content: A Rs. 1,500 'smartwatch' is a fitness band with a larger screen. It will count steps. It will show notifications. It will not make calls independently. It will look like an Apple Watch from approximately 8 feet away. If that's what you want — buy it. But know what you're buying. A genuine smartwatch with GPS, AMOLED display, and standalone calling starts around Rs. 6,000 in Pakistan. Below that, you're in fitness-band-in-a-watch-costume territory. (We sell both. We label them honestly. The Rs. 1,500 one says 'fitness tracker.' The Rs. 8,999 one says 'Smart Watch Series X with GPS.' The price tells you which is which. The description confirms it. Shop accordingly.)

sections.text: Chargers and cables — the most counterfeited category, period

sections.content: A genuine 25W Samsung fast charger has specific internals — a power management IC, proper isolation between high and low voltage sides, thermal protection. A fake one has whatever the factory had lying around and a prayer. Fake chargers destroy phone batteries. They overheat. They occasionally catch fire. (This is not hyperbole. Counterfeit chargers are a documented fire hazard according to Electrical Safety First, a UK government-backed safety organization.) Spend the extra Rs. 500 for a branded charger. Your Rs. 200,000 phone deserves better than a Rs. 300 charger whose brand name is 'SAMSNUG' in slightly wrong font.

sections.text: The warranty problem nobody talks about

sections.content: Most electronics sold online in Pakistan come with 'seller warranty' — which means the seller promises to fix or replace it. This is not the same as manufacturer warranty. Samsung Pakistan will not honour a warranty claim on a phone bought from an unauthorised online seller. Neither will Apple. Neither will any major brand. Seller warranty works when the seller is honest and still in business. It fails when the seller has changed their WhatsApp number and their Instagram page now sells real estate in Gwadar.

Our approach at BazaarNow: if a product arrives damaged or stops working within the warranty period stated on the product page, we replace it or refund it. No arguing. No 'send it to the service centre in Karachi and wait 4 weeks.' We handle it. This is not because we're saints. It's because we've calculated that replacing 3% of products costs less than losing repeat customers. Self-interest, honestly applied, is the most reliable form of customer service. Look for stores that understand this math. Avoid stores that don't.

You need it today. Right now. For a presentation. For a trip. For a gift exchange that starts in 3 hours. Our delivery takes 2-4 working days. Go to Hafeez Centre. Go to Singapore Plaza. Touch the product. Pay the in-person premium. It's worth it for same-day certainty. Come back to us for the accessories, the spare charger, the second pair of earbuds for the gym. We'll still be here, shipping in 2-4 working days, not promising same-day delivery because we know we can't do it reliably. There's honour in knowing your limits. (There's also math. Failed same-day delivery promises cost more in customer trust than they earn in orders.)

Also: don't buy electronics online without confirming the voltage. Some imported gadgets run on 110V. Pakistan runs on 220V. Plugging a 110V device into a Pakistani socket without a step-down transformer is how you create an indoor firework display. A very brief one. Followed by a very long silence. Check the specs before ordering. If the listing doesn't mention voltage — ask. If the seller can't answer — don't buy.

sections.content: We wrote a [whole post about COD](/blog/cash-on-delivery-pakistan-online-shopping) and a [whole post about JazzCash payments](/blog/how-to-pay-with-jazzcash-online-pakistan). Make sure the AirPods connect to your phone and the charger doesn't emit 'fzzzzt.' Once you've verified the store delivers genuine products — switch to advance payment. You get 5% off. On a Rs. 8,000 order, that's Rs. 400. That's a free pair of basic earphones. Or two Zinger burgers. Or half a tank of petrol. These are real economic tradeoffs. We respect them.

items.q: Are online electronics in Pakistan genuine?
items.a: Some are. Some aren't. The difference comes down to the store. Genuine stores list actual specifications (Bluetooth version, driver size, battery mAh). Fake stores list adjectives ('crystal clear sound,' 'amazing quality,' 'premium feel'). Buy from stores that list specs, not vibes. Our [electronics collection](/category/electronics) lists specs on every product page.

items.q: What if the electronics product I receive is defective?
items.a: You have 7 days to return it. Don't accept a defective product with COD — tell the rider, contact us, we'll replace it. If you paid in advance, we refund to your JazzCash, EasyPaisa, or bank account within 3-5 working days. See our [return policy](/returns) for the full details.

items.q: Are electronics more expensive online than in physical stores?
items.a: Usually the opposite. Physical stores in Pakistan add 20-40% margin to cover rent in malls like Packages or Emporium. Online stores have lower overhead. The Rs. 3,499 earbuds you see online might be Rs. 4,500 in a physical shop. The tradeoff is delivery time. You pay less but wait 2-4 days. That's the entire e-commerce value proposition in one sentence.

items.q: Can I get original Apple/Samsung products online in Pakistan?
items.a: Original products exist online — but verify the seller. Ask for the serial number and check it on the brand's warranty website before paying. If the seller refuses to share the serial number, that's your answer. BazaarNow lists whether products are OEM, brand-authorised, or third-party on the product page. We don't sell 'original' AirPods at Rs. 2,000 because original AirPods don't cost Rs. 2,000 anywhere on Earth.

items.a: COD for first orders. Always. Inspect the product before paying. For repeat orders from a trusted store, advance payment (JazzCash, EasyPaisa, bank transfer) gets you 5% off at BazaarNow. The 5% adds up — on electronics orders, which tend to be higher-value, the savings are meaningful.
